title: The Amnesty at the Conquest of Mecca
text:
For years the Quraysh, the ruling tribe of Mecca, had persecuted the Prophet Muhammad and his followers, driven them out of the city, and fought them in a series of wars. In January 630, after the Quraysh's allies broke a truce, Muhammad marched on Mecca with an army of about ten thousand.

The city barely resisted. According to Ibn Ishaq's biography, preserved in the edition of Ibn Hisham, Muhammad had announced beforehand that anyone who stayed in their own house with the door closed, took refuge in the house of the Meccan leader Abu Sufyan, or entered the sacred mosque would be safe.

After entering the city and clearing the idols from the Kaaba, he stood at its door and addressed the assembled Quraysh, many of whom had fought him for years. Ibn Ishaq reports that he asked them what they thought he would do with them. They answered that they expected good from a generous brother and the son of a generous brother. He told them: "Go, you are free."

A small number of individuals were excluded from the amnesty, and some of them were later pardoned too. Many former enemies, including Abu Sufyan, became Muslims and leaders in the community.
lesson: The moment you have power over old enemies is the moment generosity counts most. Forgiveness then can turn opponents into allies.
source: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah, as edited by Ibn Hisham
